title_clean: We Tried Futures & Options in Crypto and Made 45% ROI in 1 Month
summary: A beginner trader ran crypto options on an unregulated exchange with a 2,000 USDT trading credit and returned ~45% in a month. Walks through crypto option mechanics: option-chain UI, wallet-vs-margin allocation, auto square-off, transfer fees, and P&L-report flaws.
lessons: Crypto premiums are ultra-high: the same far-OTM strikes that pay pennies on index options paid thousands of dollars.
Exchange P&L reports counted premium credits as profit; true P&L must be computed from wallet balance minus deposits.
Funds sit in a wallet and must be allocated to trading; unallocated losing positions get auto squared-off.
Cross-exchange USDT transfers cost $10-50 in network fees - a real drag for small accounts.

title_clean: Salaried Person in F&O, Presumptive Taxation, Turnover Calculation, Audit Requirement
summary: Tax-expert Q&A on F&O taxation: government employees should obtain departmental permission; salaried traders file ITR-3 (ITR-4 under presumptive); F&O turnover is absolute profit plus absolute loss plus options premium; audit threshold 10 crore; losses must be filed by the due date.
lessons: F&O turnover = |profits| + |losses| + options premium received - miscalculation cascades into audit and presumptive-tax errors.
Audit is not mandatory below 10 crore turnover even with large losses; audit with a loss is precaution, not obligation.
File by the due date to carry forward losses - belated returns forfeit set-off.
Incidental expenses (data, advisory, depreciation, proportionate rent) are deductible if directly related to trading and not paid in cash.

event_claims.claim: F&O audit threshold is 10 crore turnover because transactions run through banking channels (otherwise 2 crore)
Presumptive taxation requires turnover below 2 crore and deemed profit of 6% (digital) or 8% (non-digital)
Losses cannot be carried forward from a belated return filed after the due date
Under presumptive taxation, earlier-year losses cannot be set off against deemed income

title_clean: Equity Options vs Crypto Options - Complete Guide

title_clean: How an Option Buyer Paid 1 Lakh Premium But Lost 13 Lakhs
summary: Cautionary anatomy of a stock-option buyer: an IndusInd 450-strike put expired out-of-the-money by last-traded price but in-the-money by the weighted-average close, forcing physical settlement and an auction-market buyback near 480 - a ~13.5 lakh loss on a ~1 lakh premium.
lessons: 'Limited risk' buying is false for physically-settled stock options that expire ITM - losses can multiply many times the premium.
Closing price is the last half-hour weighted average, not the last traded price; strikes near the money hinge on this distinction.
Never carry stock options into expiry: square off at least a day early, or trade index options which are cash-settled.

event_claims.claim: IndusInd Bank December-2021 expiry (30 Dec): last traded price 451.95 but closing (weighted average) 449.65, making the 450 put ITM by 0.35
The buyer held 45,000 quantity bought around 2 rupees (~1 lakh premium) and faced auction-market buyback around 480 on 4 January 2022, a ~30 rupee/ share loss (~13.5 lakh)
If delivery cannot be met and no auction seller exists, the exchange levies a 20% penalty on contract value (~1.5 lakh on a 7-8 lakh contract)
T+2 settlement timeline: broker must buy in the auction market two days after expiry to fulfil delivery

quotes: Always remember, information is wealth... the risk can be unlimited even if you are an option buyer.

title_clean: TCS Trading Strategy Ahead of Q3 Results (Live Trade)
summary: Pre-earnings TCS structure built live: a 1:3 call ratio (buy 3800C, sell three 4000C) with the extra credit spent on two OTM calls to cap risk, plus a 3700/3500 put spread for margin - breakevens 3678/4122, max profit 36,000, max loss 53,000 on ~1.5 lakh margin; sells the buyback-driven IV spike.
lessons: Sell event-inflated IV rather than buy it: the buyback announcement spiked premiums, and that spike was the trade.
Ratio spreads monetize a bounded directional view - long the move, short the overshoot, credit-funded wings for limited risk.
Hedged legs slash margin: a multi-lot structure ran on ~1.5 lakh because every short had a long against it.
